file_description: Daily Gas Production - Average daily gas production rate by field
data_format: WIDE format - one row per field-month with average daily rate
priority: MEDIUM - Useful for validation and rate analysis
use_case: Validate monthly totals, track production rates, calculate uptime/downtime, identify production interruptions

field_descriptions.gas_production_avg_daily_mm3: Average daily gas production rate in million cubic meters per day (Mm3/day) for the given month. Arithmetic mean of daily production over all producing days in the month.
field_descriptions.time_index: Year-month identifier in YYYY-MM format for time series analysis
field_descriptions.field_id: Unique field identifier - matches field_id in monthly production and field shapes
field_descriptions.basin: Sedimentary basin (Neuquina, Golfo San Jorge, Austral, Noroeste, Cuyana)

unit_notes.mm3_per_day: Million cubic meters per day (Mm3/day) - average daily rate. Note: Mm3 = 10^6 m3
unit_notes.mm3: Million cubic meters - if converting to monthly total, multiply by days in month
unit_notes.gas_conversion_mcf: Mm3/day to Mcf/day (thousand cubic feet): multiply by 35.3147
unit_notes.gas_conversion_scf: Mm3/day to scf/day (standard cubic feet): multiply by 35,314,700
unit_notes.gas_conversion_mscf: Mm3/day to Mscf/day (thousand scf): multiply by 35,314.7
unit_notes.monthly_validation: To validate: gas_production_avg_daily_mm3 * days_in_month ≈ monthly_total_mm3 from gas_field_production file

calculated_metrics.monthly_expected_mm3: gas_production_avg_daily_mm3 * days_in_month - Expected monthly production if running at full capacity
calculated_metrics.production_uptime_fraction: actual_monthly_mm3 / (gas_production_avg_daily_mm3 * days_in_month) - Fraction of time actually producing. <1.0 indicates downtime.
calculated_metrics.downtime_days_equivalent: (1 - uptime_fraction) * days_in_month - Equivalent days of downtime in the month
calculated_metrics.is_intermittent_production: uptime_fraction < 0.7 - Binary flag for fields with significant downtime
calculated_metrics.gas_oil_ratio_proxy: gas_production_avg_daily_mm3 / oil_production_avg_daily_m3 - Approximate GOR when paired with oil data (needs unit conversion)

data_quality_validation.monthly_total_check: Compare daily avg * days to monthly total from gas_field_production file. Should match within ~5% unless significant downtime.
data_quality_validation.zero_production: Zero values may indicate: (1) field shut-in, (2) maintenance, (3) no production that month, (4) oil field with minimal associated gas, (5) data not reported
data_quality_validation.outlier_detection: Sudden spikes or drops in daily rate month-to-month may indicate: pipeline capacity changes, new gas processing, compression issues, or data errors
data_quality_validation.consistency_check: Gas production daily rate should be relatively stable unless gas processing/compression changes. Large variations warrant investigation.
data_quality_validation.associated_vs_non_associated: Gas-only fields should have consistent rates. Oil fields with associated gas may have more variation tied to oil production.

technical_notes.average_calculation: This is arithmetic mean of daily gas production over the month. Does not account for days with zero production vs no production.
technical_notes.uptime_analysis: Comparing daily average to monthly total reveals production uptime. Gas fields often have 85-98% uptime due to continuous flow requirements.
technical_notes.rate_vs_volume: Daily rate (Mm3/day) measures intensity of production. Monthly volume (Mm3) measures total production. Both needed for complete analysis.
technical_notes.validation_importance: Cross-checking daily rates against monthly totals is critical quality control. Mismatches indicate data errors, downtime, or gas flaring.
technical_notes.decline_curve_analysis: Daily rates more useful for decline curve analysis than monthly totals. Shows gas production rate changes over time.
technical_notes.comparison_to_us_units: US oilfield uses Mcf/day (thousand cubic feet per day) or MMcf/day (million cubic feet per day) instead of Mm3/day. 1 Mm3/day = 35,314.7 Mcf/day = 35.3147 MMcf/day.
technical_notes.gas_compression: Gas production rates can be limited by compression capacity. Sudden drops may indicate compressor issues rather than reservoir decline.
technical_notes.flaring_consideration: Production rate here is PRODUCED gas, not SALES gas. Some produced gas may be flared, vented, or consumed on-site.
technical_notes.associated_gas_dynamics: For oil fields, gas production follows oil production. For gas fields, production is primary objective and more consistent.

data_integration.join_key: field_id + year + month - join to monthly production data
validation_workflow: 3. Calculate expected monthly = daily avg * days in month
6. Flag fields with uptime < 70% for investigation
data_integration.complementary_data: Use with monthly production totals to calculate uptime, identify production interruptions, and validate data quality
data_integration.cross_validation_with_oil: For associated gas, cross-check with oil production daily averages. GOR should be relatively consistent month-to-month.

use_cases.data_validation: Primary use is validating monthly gas production totals. Daily avg * days should match monthly total within 5-10%.
use_cases.uptime_calculation: Calculate field operating uptime by comparing actual monthly to expected (daily * days). Identify reliability and compression issues.
use_cases.rate_analysis: Track gas production rate trends over time. Identify decline rates, compression capacity impacts, processing facility changes.
use_cases.anomaly_detection: Sudden changes in daily rate indicate production events: compression changes, pipeline restrictions, facility shutdowns, or data errors.
use_cases.operator_performance: Compare uptime across operators to identify best practices and operational efficiency differences.
use_cases.gas_oil_ratio_tracking: When combined with oil daily production, track field GOR evolution over time (important for reservoir management).

limitations.no_well_level: This is field-level average only. Does not show individual well contributions.
limitations.averaging_masks_detail: Daily average smooths out intra-month variation. Doesn't show when production occurred or rate fluctuations.
limitations.zero_ambiguity: Zero production could mean shut-in field, gas flared/vented instead of produced, or missing data. Cannot distinguish without additional info.
limitations.no_pressure_breakdown: Unlike monthly gas_field_production file, this does not separate by pressure category (high/medium/low). Total gas only.
limitations.produced_vs_sales: This shows produced gas. Actual sales gas may be lower due to flaring, venting, fuel use, or processing losses.

typical_values.small_gas_field_mm3_day: 0.01-0.1 Mm3/day typical for small gas field or oil field with associated gas (10,000-100,000 m3/day)
typical_values.medium_gas_field_mm3_day: 0.1-1.0 Mm3/day for medium gas field (100,000-1,000,000 m3/day = 3.5-35 MMcf/day)
typical_values.large_gas_field_mm3_day: 1.0-10.0 Mm3/day for large gas field or Vaca Muerta gas development (35-350 MMcf/day)
typical_values.giant_gas_field_mm3_day: >10.0 Mm3/day for major gas fields (>350 MMcf/day). Top Argentina fields produce 20+ Mm3/day.
typical_values.expected_uptime: Gas fields: 90-98% (continuous production preferred). Oil fields with associated gas: 80-95% (tied to oil production).
typical_values.unconventional_vaca_muerta: Vaca Muerta gas wells can produce 0.01-0.5 Mm3/day initially, declining to 0.001-0.05 Mm3/day after 2-3 years.

example_analysis.validation_check_python: is_valid = abs(monthly_total_mm3 - daily_avg_mm3 * days_in_month) / monthly_total_mm3 < 0.10  # Within 10%
example_analysis.gor_estimation_python:
# GOR in scf/bbl (requires unit conversion)
gor_scf_bbl = (gas_mm3_day * 35314700) / (oil_m3_day * 6.28981)

opgee_relevance.gas_production_opgee: For OPGEE, this daily rate data helps validate annual production inputs and assess field stability.
opgee_relevance.gor_calculation: Combined with oil daily production, can calculate field GOR - critical OPGEE input parameter.
opgee_relevance.flaring_estimation: Difference between produced gas (this file) and sales gas (from plant processing file) indicates flaring/venting levels.
opgee_relevance.production_consistency: Uptime analysis reveals field operational stability - affects OPGEE energy consumption and emissions estimates.
